newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian evades security to give emperor letter.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian evades security to give emperor letter.

text.p: A Brazilian woman of Japanese descent slipped by security for visiting Japanese Emperor Akihito on Thursday and tried to give him a letter before being pulled away by guards, witnesses said.

Shizuka Honma, thought to be in her 60s, broke through a security line to give Akihito, who was inside a car, a letter that she claimed proved her lineage to Japan's imperial family, a Reuter photographer on the spot said.
Honma, who walked right up to the car, was taken away by guards. It was not immediately clear if she was arrested.
Akihito, who remained inside his car throughout the incident, looked curiously at the woman, who had just come from a welcoming reception for the emperor and Empress Michiko.
The imperial couple are halfway through a 10-day visit to Brazil. Sao Paulo, which has some 1.3 million Japanese descendants, is home to the largest Japanese community outside Japan.

Throughout their trip, the imperial couple has been protected by Japanese police rather than the imperial guards normally used on foreign visits. The change was attributed to growing security concerns in Japan after the four-month hostage drama at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru.
